transcript:
Header: 2027-06-03 15:00 PDT | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), Evan (BlueWave CTO), Sofia (ML Eng), Marcus (Infra), Aisha (PM)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side — I'm Jordan, I'm AE, Priya and Liam are our SE folks, we'll focus the call on scoping the POC SLOs for latency and throughput.

[00:18] Evan: Great, thanks. We want to be explicit about success criteria before we start. our main concern is end-user latency on the chat endpoints and also steady-state throughput for our nightly batch generative jobs.

[00:33] Priya: Awesome, can you walk through current traffic? what are RPS, typical prompt lengths, and which endpoints are highest priority?

[00:45] Sofia: Sure — two primary endpoints: 1) "assist-chat" for interactive product help, avg prompt 64 tokens, expected 30–120 RPS peak per region, 95th percentile concurrent requests around 45; 2) "doc-summarize-batch" for internal batch runs, avg prompt 512 tokens, we run large batches overnight, throughput matters there. We also have a smaller rerank endpoint for search.

[01:12] Marcus: infra constraints: most prod runs in GCP us-west1, but we want to test private deployment in our VPC for data residency later. for the POC we can open a staging VPC or allow ephemeral peering.

[01:28] Liam: Noted. When we talk about latency SLOs, are you thinking TTFT (time to first token) or end-to-end completion time? some folks use TPOT or tokens-per-second for throughput.

[01:42] Evan: We heard TTFT is the most important for perceived snappiness in the UI. but we also want to track token generation rate — especially p95 of tokens-per-second for the batch job.

[01:55] Priya: Ok, quick definitions to align: TTFT = time from request to when the first token (or first byte) is emitted — this is the user-perceived latency for streaming chat. TPOT in our notes we use to mean "time-per-token" or conversely tokens-per-second; for reporting we can surface both (time-per-token and tokens/sec). For SLOs we recommend p95/p99 for TTFT and p95 for steady-state per-token times or tokens/sec.

[02:25] Jordan: To make it concrete, what targets would be acceptable for BlueWave?

[02:32] Evan: For the chat endpoint, p95 TTFT under 200ms would be a stretch goal, p95 under 300ms is acceptable. p99 under 500ms. For longer prompts I'm ok with higher numbers but want them documented. For the batch job, we'd like throughput > 20 tokens/sec per GPU or equivalent, or a guarantee on total throughput to finish within our nightly window.

[02:58] Priya: That's helpful. For POC we typically run three benchmark classes: cold-first-request (no warm cache), warm steady-state (with KV/prefix cache filled), and scaled concurrency tests. We'll measure TTFT, TPOT (ms/token), and tokens/sec, and report p50/p95/p99. We'll also capture tail latencies and error rates.

[03:18] Sofia: what's your measurement methodology? we care about reproducibility and accounting for retries/queueing.

[03:25] Priya: We'll provide a load generator (wrk-like) and a reproducible script. plan: 1) ingest your representative prompt set (you'll share ~200 prompts representative of our product), 2) run single-req latency tests across prompt lengths (64, 256, 512 tokens), 3) run steady-state generation tests for N seconds capturing first token and token rate, 4) run concurrency sweep 1–200 RPS to find p95/p99 inflection points. We'll also vary batch sizes and quantization configs if using dedicated nodes.

[03:57] Marcus: will you include profiling that attributes time to networking vs model compute vs pre/post-processing?

[04:03] Priya: Yes — our telemetry tags request phases: routing, network, model-init, kv-cache lookup, kernel exec (compute), and post-processing. For hosted tests we also show per-token cost. For private/dedicated we can drop network overhead but we'll still report host-level metrics.

[04:22] Evan: about KV cache/prefix caching: some of our prompts have long contexts and we want caching to reduce TTFT. how do you measure cache hit benefits?

[04:30] Priya: We'll run paired tests: cold run (empty cache) vs cache-warmed run (preload token KV). measure delta on TTFT and per-token times. we'll capture cache-hit ratios and show how much prefix caching reduces compute and tail latency.

[04:46] Jordan: ok lets draft a candidate SLO table now so we have something to iterate on.

[04:52] Priya: Proposed SLOs (draft):
- Chat (64 token avg prompt): p95 TTFT <= 300ms, p99 TTFT <= 550ms, p95 steady-state tokens/sec >= 40 (for X hardware profile)
- Long-chat (256–512 tokens): p95 TTFT <= 450ms, p99 <= 900ms (due to longer decode time)
- Batch summarize (512 tokens avg): throughput >= 20 tokens/sec per GPU or job completes within nightly window (to be specified)
- Error rate < 0.5% and tail p99 error handling documented

[05:28] Evan: The chat p95 300ms is acceptable, we'll aim to tune towards 200ms if feasible. how do you map these to hardware choices?

[05:35] Priya: We'll produce benchmark profiles for a few model variants and hardware: A) hosted multi-tenant on V100/A100-like, B) dedicated reserved instances (A100x2), C) private deployment with q8/4 quantization on Ampere-ish GPUS. We'll also test with batching on/off and different max tokens. Each profile will list observed TTFT/TPOT, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.

[05:59] Marcus: For private testing we need to ensure keys/KMS and audit logs are retained — can the POC run in our staging VPC?

[06:06] Jordan: Yes we'll support staging VPC peering for the benchmark window; Priya will coordinate with Marcus on access and required security docs. we'll provide SOC2/ISO paperwork.

[06:16] Sofia: For measurement, do you run p95/p99 across the entire run or per-minute windows? we saw weird spikes in our last infra tests.

[06:24] Priya: We report both overall p50/p95/p99 and sliding-window percentiles (1m/5m) to identify transient spikes. We'll include histograms and raw samples so you can compute other aggregations.

[06:36] Liam: Another point — TTFT depends a lot on cold-start vs warm. for LL models with KV cache warmed TTFT can be <100ms for small prompts; cold can be multiple hundreds. We'll show both numbers and recommend caching strategies.

[06:48] Evan: Good. timeline? we're hoping to get results by mid next week to present to execs on 2027-06-15.

[06:55] Jordan: Proposed timeline: this week (June 3–6) gather prompts and traffic histogram; next week (June 7–11) run benchmarks and produce preliminary results; Jun 14–15 review and refine SLOs and sign pilot SOW. That fits your exec date?

[07:11] Evan: yes, that works.

[07:14] Priya: We'll also include measurement of cost tradeoffs and batching recommendations (max batch size, target latency vs cost curves). For example we might show that increasing batch size from 1 to 4 reduces cost/token by 30% but increases p95 TTFT by 40ms — you'll be able to pick the sweet spot.

[07:33] Sofia: are you able to run token-level profiling to show where compute hot paths are? e.g., attention vs matmul vs softmax kernels?

[07:40] Priya: Yes, for the dedicated/private runs we can export a breakdown of time spent in kernels vs pre/post processing; for hosted multi-tenant we provide an aggregated breakdown (some kernel names may be obfuscated in multi-tenant environment).

[07:53] Marcus: security checklist — SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, data retention policy. we'll need SOC2 docs before any private deployment.

[08:01] Jordan: We'll attach the security pack and SOC2 report in the follow-up email.

[08:06] Evan: One last question — how do you measure TPOT exactly? we want to ensure we're not mixing tokens/sec with wall clock generation time.

[08:13] Priya: TPOT we'll report as ms/token (average and percentiles) and also tokens/sec (steady-state) as complementary metrics. ms/token is computed as (decode time)/(number of tokens generated) over steady windows, whereas tokens/sec is tokens emitted per second in steady-steady state. both useful: ms/token maps to CPU/GPU time, tokens/sec maps to throughput capacity.

[08:34] Jordan: Great. Quick recap of agreed success criteria:
- Two priority endpoints: chat (64 tokens) and batch (512 tokens)
- Draft SLOs: chat p95 TTFT <= 300ms, p99 <= 550ms; batch throughput >= 20 tokens/sec per GPU or finish nightly run within window
- Measurement plan: scripted benchmark (cold/warm/steady), sliding-window percentiles, kernel/phase profiling, per-run histograms
- Timeline: prompts & traffic histogram by 2027-06-06, benchmark week 2027-06-07..11, results review 2027-06-14/15

[08:58] Evan: Sounds good. we'll upload prompts and histogram later today.

[09:02] Jordan: Ok I'll follow up with pilot SOW and Priya will share the load scripts. thanks all.

[09:07] End: informal chat about next call scheduling and internal owners.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had a few name errors and occasional dropped punctuation; speaker turns are approximate.
